lessons.title: Choose the abstraction by the question
lessons.physicalIntuition: Detail is valuable only if it contains the mechanism being investigated. Averaging is ideal for low-frequency plant work; switched behavior is required for pulses; device models are needed for switching loss/edge stress.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Map each question to required state/event bandwidth and compare it with what averaging, ideal switches, ABM, and device models retain. Establish validation oracles appropriate to the rung.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Every testbench declares abstraction, included/excluded effects, and why that rung is sufficient. Build upward only after lower-rung invariants pass.
lessons.transferQuestion: Why is a transistor-level model a poor first tool for debugging scheduler fairness?

lessons.title: ABM building blocks for controllers
lessons.physicalIntuition: Each ideal function needs memory, delay, thresholds, and saturation made explicit enough to avoid impossible instantaneous circular behavior.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Define piecewise comparator guards, Schmitt thresholds, latch truth table, timer inequalities, delayed events, and controlled-switch state equations. Smooth only the numerical discontinuity that is intentionally approximated and document its scale.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Use inspectable hierarchical subcircuits and named internal nodes. Avoid undocumented syntax and verify every ABM expression against the official user guide and target version.
assumptions: behavioral blocks omit semiconductor overdrive/metastability unless modeled
lessons.transferQuestion: Which state element breaks a comparator-to-switch-to-comparator zero-delay loop and what timing does it add?

lessons.title: Transient setup and convergence debugging
lessons.physicalIntuition: A solver must reconcile nonlinear states and discontinuous events. Unrealistically perfect switches, missing DC paths, and simultaneous zero-delay decisions can make the mathematics ill-conditioned even when the intended idea is simple.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Relate maximum step to the shortest pulse/delay and integration error, then perform step/tolerance sensitivity. Add physically/behaviorally justified finite resistance, hysteresis, delay, or weak DC path rather than random numerical patches.
lessons.modelingConsequence: The debugging lab demands evidence, likely cause, correction, and revalidation. A smaller step or relaxed tolerance is never accepted without explaining its physical/numerical effect.
assumptions: specific solver settings depend on installed PSpice release
lessons.transferQuestion: How do you distinguish comparator chatter from a trapezoidal numerical oscillation?

lessons.title: Sweeps, mismatch, measurements, and loop injection
lessons.physicalIntuition: One nominal waveform cannot reveal sensitivity. Measurements need definitions and windows, and randomness needs a seed/distribution.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Define cursor/window metrics for average, RMS, peak-to-peak, event frequency, phase separation, recovery time, and sharing error. Specify parameter distributions and preserve seeds. Use a valid injection topology for linear loop response.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Testbenches emit raw signals plus measured values and scenario metadata. Separate controller-only test stimuli from full power-stage tests to isolate faults.
assumptions: Monte Carlo distributions are synthetic unless sourced
lessons.transferQuestion: Why must a per-phase switching-frequency metric specify its time window in variable-frequency COT?
